The core decisions hold up: one block and one hook, a pure integer kernel, a Q14/Q28 cone test, a doubled-coordinate slab segment test, a canonical hysteresis bit, an oracle-proven pair cache, counted work, and pending-intent columns. They are probed on the 4.7.2 editor binary and the alternatives are genuinely weighed. The problem statement, rationale and Consequences are honest, including the admission in D12.6 that the budget does not fit. What passes: the engine is stamped 4.7.2 with Knowledge Risk HIGH, post-cutoff APIs are listed and the probes are dated. All 57 TR rows that requirements-traceability.md maps to ADR-0017 are addressed, and all 46 TR-emitter rows are classified (42 decided, 15 shared, 9 owned elsewhere). Fault domain 6 matches the registry table. The rects_in / QueryBuffer.spans / version_epoch / changed_region usage matches ADR-0014 sections 5 and 6. The hook edges match ADR-0012 and ADR-0015, and the restore_after list matches ADR-0016 position 6. ADR-0004 lets each block number its own key kinds, so kind 1 is legal. Three blocking problems remain. (T1) The save-equivalence (G4) argument for post_restore is incomplete. Hooks ordered after emitter.place can write upstream blocks on the snapshot tick, for example Interaction calling Graph M6 (salvage_node). Re-running the hysteresis in post_restore can then rewrite a canonical lit bit. (T2) D10.2 has registrants re-register (E6) from their own post_restore. That is a cross-block canonical write, which ADR-0016 section 4.2 forbids. (T3) A PLAYER-origin set_switch has no reach, NOT_LIT or loco_state check anywhere on the authoritative path. Beyond those, several cross-ADR assumptions do not match the sibling drafts on disk: M14 is not allowed in the INIT scope, BODY_COORD_LIMIT does not exist, there is no node_base read and no template emitter-placement accessor, ControllerView names differ, and the published occ_origin is missing. These need amendment rows, not redesign.

findings.text: The G4 argument (D14.4 items 2-3, D9.5(b), D14.2) has a gap. It assumes post_restore re-derives the table from the same upstream state that the last emitter.place saw. That is not true when a hook ordered after emitter.place writes an upstream block on the snapshot tick. Concrete case: Interaction's hook runs after emitter.place (ADR-0017's own assumption on ADR-0020). It may call Graph M6 salvage_node, an immediate mutator allowed in HOOK scope (ADR-0012 scope table, and its assumption on ADR-0021 'M5/M6/M7 also from an Interaction hook'). The live run's table at the end of tick T still counts that lamp. The restored run's post_restore reads node_state SALVAGED, so the lamp is not live and act_lux drops. D14.2 then runs 'W6 with the hysteresis' and LitHysteresis.next(1, act') can write 0 into the canonical lit bit. The P2 validate at T+1 then accepts a lit-only verb in one run and rejects it NOT_LIT in the other. If act at T+1 sits between LIT_OFF_PM and LIT_ON_PM, the divergence persists. Writing a persisted column in post_restore also breaks ADR-0016 section 4.2. The 'idempotent' claim only holds for an identical act, and the late-hook mutation removes that.
findings.amendment: (1) In D9.5(b) and D14.2, make post_restore copy the lit bit verbatim and never call LitHysteresis.next. Only lux_pm, act_lux_pm, top_emitter_id and the record fields are recomputed. (2) Restate D14.4 (2)-(3): derived values rebuilt in post_restore reflect end-of-tick upstream state, which can differ from what the last run saw by any write made by a hook ordered after emitter.place. Only canonical-backed reads (lit, beam_of, subject_headroom, the registration set) are G4-exact before the first run. lux, top_emitter, output_of, r_lit_of, r_off_of and section_emission may differ for one run. Then add a rule plus a lint or test that no validate and no hook ordered before emitter.place decides state on those derived reads. Alternative to the read restriction: persist the per-emitter live/output inputs the last run used. (3) Add mandatory KRN-RST-05 fixtures to D2.5's list: Interaction's hook calls M6 on a lit lamp's node on the snapshot tick, and a late hook changes loco_state to DEAD on the snapshot tick.

findings.text: D10.2 says registrants (Interaction, Horror, loot spawners) 're-register idempotently in their own post_restore (restore_after allows it)', and the ADR-0020 cross-ADR row repeats it. E6/E7/E8 write canonical emitter.state columns (D2.5) and must begin with scope.open_for (D3.4, EMT-05). Under ADR-0016 section 4.2 and its line 347, post_restore holds no WriteScope and must never write another block. ADR-0016 (lines 392 and 418) already moved Interaction to 'detect at post_restore, repair in the hook'. This text cannot be implemented and conflicts with a sibling. It also muddies Open Question 4.
findings.amendment: Rewrite D10.2: registrations are canonical and restore verbatim, so a well-formed save needs no re-registration. A registrant detects drift in its own post_restore without writing, and repairs it in its first hook run through E6/E7/E8. The pending columns of D2.5 absorb the repair with at most a one-run lag. Apply the same wording to the ADR-0020 and ADR-0022/0023 rows in Cross-ADR Assumptions. Close Open Question 4 on that basis, keeping 'no edge from Interaction' and 'Interaction ordered after emitter.place'.

findings.text: D3.2/D3.3 give PLAYER-origin set_switch the validation order NO_SUCH_EMITTER, NOT_SWITCHABLE, COOLDOWN only. The GDD (EM set_switch row; Interaction line 136, IA-37) says 'NOT_LIT is Interaction's own precondition'. Under IA-3 and ADR-0002, a command type has exactly one validate, and set_switch's validate is the Emitter's. The payload is {emitter_id} only. No step of the authoritative pipeline therefore checks reach or focus, NOT_LIT, or a DEAD/DOWNED/STAGGERED actor for a fixture switch, although toggle_beam has NOT_ACTIONABLE. A PLAYER submit can switch any fixture by id from anywhere, and in VS-B a remote peer can too. Stories for the verb cannot be cut without knowing where those checks live.
findings.amendment: In D3.2, add to the PLAYER set_switch order (before COOLDOWN) a call to a pure Interaction-published precondition, for example InteractionView.verb_precondition(actor, subject_ref, verb) -> StringName, returning NOT_LIT, OUT_OF_REACH or NOT_ACTIONABLE. Its reasons pass through under VALIDATION_FAILED. This keeps IA-11(a), which forbids reading node health. State that the Emitter owns the call site and ADR-0020 owns the predicate (see the cross-ADR item). If the decision is instead that the Adapter's focus filter is sufficient, say so explicitly and record the authority consequence for VS-B.

findings.text: Acceptance gating is circular as written. 'Blocks' says no Emitter epic can start until this ADR is Accepted. D12.6 says EM-SPIKE-1 'measures each weight in the real code on both machines', and Validation Criteria says 'a hot max above 2 ms blocks Acceptance'. Scenario hot-max figures require the real W0..W7 hook, which cannot be written before acceptance. architecture.md defines S1 as a stub harness (stub Graph, emitter.place at realistic counts), so the honest gate exists but the ADR does not cite it.
findings.amendment: Split the gate the way ADR-0006 split SAVE-WRK-1. S1/EM-SPIKE-1-ACCEPT gates Accept: a release-export harness in prototypes/ or tools/bench with the shared kernel functions and a W0-W7 skeleton at the D.14 typical point, with a stated pass threshold (for example steady state at or below B with at least 15 % margin at measured weights, or a named ladder rung selected). EM-SPIKE-1-SLICE runs the real hook's S1..S8b scenario hot max and gates the Vertical Slice milestone, not Accept. Reword D12.6, R1 and Validation Criteria accordingly.

findings.text: D3.4 E1 and D5.2 have E1 call M14 set_load_request under the INIT scope at Web Map init_world (an authored-on lamp starts ARMING), and assume the deposit drains at the first power hook. ADR-0012's mutator table lists M14 as 'APPLY, HOOK' only (only M1 lists INIT), and its drain table has no INIT row. As drafted, E1 would get a refused scope for M14, and arm_tick at T_a = 'the creation tick' is undefined for a pre-tick INIT pass.
findings.amendment: Keep the assumption but make it a hard dependency in D5.2: E1 requires M14 in INIT scope and an INIT-row drain rule from ADR-0012. Define T_a for an INIT-scope creation, i.e. the tick the INIT pass is stamped with. As a fallback if ADR-0012 refuses, E1 creates authored-on Graph lamps with switch_on set and no M14 call, and the Graph seeds load_req from the template so that ARMING is unnecessary at world build.

findings.text: I-BOUNDS, the D8.3 overflow proof and the ADR-0015 assumption row cite 'BODY_COORD_LIMIT (the ADR-0015 bounds ledger)'. ADR-0015 defines no such constant. It has WORLD_COORD_LIMIT (2^22) and the prose 'a body-frame coordinate is bounded by section extents (tens of thousands of px)'. The boot invariant as written cannot be implemented. Open Question 6 half-acknowledges this.
findings.amendment: Replace BODY_COORD_LIMIT with a named, data-held bound the ADR can check, either sourced from ADR-0015 (see the cross-ADR item) or derived here from Layout facts (max section extent times max sections per body, plus the WORLD_COORD_LIMIT reorigin rule). Keep the 2^26 doubled-value requirement and have I-BOUNDS fail the boot when the bound exceeds 2^24.

findings.text: Several Layout reads that E1, D10.4 and D8.4 rely on are not in ADR-0013 as drafted. (a) node_base(section_id): ADR-0013 stores graph_ref_base but no Tier H or Tier C list exposes it. (b) The section template's emitter placements (def_id, anchor, node_ordinal, authored switch_on, subkind): ADR-0013 and ADR-0007 define no accessor. (c) D10.4 sizes section-local grids from section_rects_into, but ADR-0014 section 5 says section_rects_into answers in the BODY frame. The ADR never states the translation by section_offset, and the D8.4 lint uses the same read against section-local anchors.
findings.amendment: Add to the ADR-0013 Cross-ADR row: a Tier H node_base(section_id) -> int (0 = NONE), and a SectionTemplates accessor set for emitter placements (count plus indexed scalar getters, frozen at stage 1). In D10.4 and D8.4, state that section_rects_into results are converted to section-local px by subtracting section_offset_x/_y read in the same call, and that the data-load lint uses a template-frame double.

findings.text: The interface to ADR-0018 is incomplete. 'Enables' says ADR-0018 consumes occ_origin, and ADR-0018 (lines 112 and 410, R7) assumes the Emitter publishes occ_origin as a separate integer pair and reserves OCC_ORIGIN_MODE (FOOT). D13.1's 17 fields expose origin_x_of/origin_y_of (the chest) only. occlusion_origin(row, out_xy) is internal and no tuning row reserves the mode. Outcome D would then become an interface change, not the one-function change D5.3 promises.
findings.amendment: Add occ_origin_x_of(id) and occ_origin_y_of(id) to EmitterView for BEAM rows (foot pos_curr under FOOT; 0 for other kinds), derived in W2, and reserve EmitterTuning OCC_ORIGIN_MODE with the single value FOOT. Note in D5.3 that a previous/current pair is added only if outcome D is adopted.

findings.text: D13.1 says 'no Vector2i, which SIM-03 bans in sim'. ADR-0010 section 5.5 says the opposite: SIM-03 bans Vector2( and names Vector2i as the replacement. Separately, ADR-0019's ControllerView publishes get_chest_point(player_id) -> Vector2i, get_aim_angle and get_loco_state (get_ prefix rule, section 2.6). ADR-0017 D5.3, D3.2 and the ADR-0019 assumption row assume bare chest_point as two scalars, aim_angle and loco_state.
findings.amendment: Strike the SIM-03 claim. If EmitterView keeps scalar-pair getters, justify it as this ADR's own CNT-03/style rule. Consume ADR-0019's actual names: get_chest_point -> Vector2i is a value type, allocation-free and SIM-03-legal, and the Emitter takes .x/.y once. Update the ADR-0019 assumption row to match.

findings.text: The restore behaviour of the version cache is ambiguous and conflicts with ADR-0014. D11.4 says 'the cache is reset in post_restore, so the first W0 after a restore re-reads everything'. If reset means cleared, the first tick repeats the cold build (a C_cold hitch on top of post_restore's S6 build, and CNT-04 S6 counts change). D11.5 says 'the restore-time leaf bump is a leaf-region change ..., not ALL'. ADR-0014 section 6 stamps ALL in Layout post_restore and makes version_epoch authoritative. Because Layout's post_restore runs first in the DAG, the Emitter's cold build already sees the bumped leaves.
findings.amendment: State that post_restore, after its cold build, seeds the section cache with the current (version_epoch, static_version, leaf_version, offset, body_id) read after Layout's post_restore, so the first W0 sees no change. Delete the 'restore-time leaf bump is REGION, not ALL' sentence.

findings.text: D2.5 defines pending states, but the combinations a late hook can produce in one tick are unspecified: E6 then E7 on a pending-register row, E7 then E6 on a pending-unregister row, E8 on a pending-register row, and a second E8 on a row that already has has_pend_anchor. Each changes caps, subject_headroom and restore validation (EMITTER_RESTORE_SUBJECTS), so a story cannot be cut without it. The transition table of D3.6 covers the record lifecycle and the lit bit, not pending.
findings.amendment: Add a TRANSITIONS_PENDING table to emitter_kind.gd. E6+E7 on pending 1 drops the row with no table effect. E7 on 2 is a no-op. E6 on 2 returns to 0 with an unchanged anchor, or 0 with a pending anchor if the anchor differs, and reports DUPLICATE. E8 on pending 1 writes the applied anchor directly. A repeated E8 overwrites pend_x/pend_y. Add the cases to the D2.5 fixture list.

findings.text: Wording errors that a story would copy. (a) D14.2 'so no subject is pending when the first validate runs' (inherited from ADR-0016 V9) contradicts D2.5: rows pending at the snapshot stay pending until W3 of T+1, as in the live run. (b) D14.3 places V9 at 'DAG position 5', but the ADR-0016 table has emitter.state at position 6, and its V9 slot is post_restore while D14.3 calls EmitterVerify from restore. (c) D4.2 says the derived columns are written only inside emitter.place, but E10 (P2) and the creation mutators (any scope) also write derived record fields. (d) D6.4 says reconciliation happens 'on the tick after its phase 11 ran', but emitter.place is after graph.propagate.failure on the same tick, which is what 'never later' (TR-ftrail-041) needs.
findings.amendment: (a) Reword to 'the pending set equals the live run's at T+1'. (b) Say position 6, slot restore (EmitterVerify) plus post_restore (rebuild). (c) List E10 and the creation mutators as the only out-of-hook derived writers. (d) Say 'in the same tick, after the failure hook completes'.

findings.text: Mandatory block callables and call sites are missing. default_state is mandatory (ADR-0003 section 2, line 97) and D2.1 does not specify it, while ADR-0016 asks each owner for a default_state its own restore accepts. E9 create_seat_beam is called from 'the new-game step' and E4 bind_beam 'once at new game', but no owner or order relative to Web Map's E1/E10 is named.
findings.amendment: In D2.1, add default_state: empty columns, next_emitter_id 1, last_place_tick -1, fault_step_seen -1, passing EmitterVerify. Name the E9/E4 call site and its order relative to E1/E10 (see the cross-ADR item on ADR-0026).

findings.text: HOT-01 scoping. D6.4 reads LayoutView.anchor_geometry (Tier C, allocates, per ADR-0013) and FailureSlice-driven creation inside W1. The Implementation Guidelines tag '_hook_place and its W-step helpers' ## @hot, so the fault-glow creation path would trip HOT-01 or CNT-01 whenever a glow is created.
findings.amendment: State that FAULT_GLOW row creation and removal, E1/E2 and slot-store insert/remove are untagged cold helpers called from the tagged W1. Scope CNT-01 to ticks with no structural change, or have the 600-tick fixture include a steady fault set.

findings.text: Traceability ownership error: the 'Shared' table lists TR-interact-038 with ADR-0012 as the other owner. ADR-0012's own row hands the Interaction hook budget to 'ADR-0017/0020'.
findings.amendment: Change the other owner of TR-interact-038 to ADR-0020 (the Interaction hook's own budget and worst-case load). This ADR keeps the Emitter's share and lit() as a table lookup.

findings.text: Right-sizing for a solo MVP. Two slot stores, per-section point grids, stride-K pair rows, static_epoch mover sweeps, an always-on tally, 22 fault codes and an 8-rule lint pack are justified only by a D.14 cost model whose weights are unverified. The Migration Plan already builds the brute-force oracle path first (step 6) but makes the optimised step 7 unconditional.
findings.amendment: Make Migration step 7 (grids, pair rows, static_epoch) conditional on step 6 measured against B on the S1 harness. If the oracle/cold-build path meets B with margin at the typical point, ship it and keep steps 7 and onward as ladder rungs behind the same API. Keep the transparency fuzz as the entry condition for step 7.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0016's assumption on ADR-0017 ('emitter.place is ordered after the Interaction hook that repairs subject drift') and its Open Question 5 contradict ADR-0017 D3.1 and Open Question 4. ADR-0017 declares no edge from Interaction and orders Interaction after emitter.place, because E3 at the landing tick and the D2.5 late-hook semantics depend on it. ADR-0016's V9 row also says 'no subject pending at the first validate', which D2.5 makes false by design.
cross_adr.amendment: Close Open Question 5 with ADR-0017's position: registrations are canonical; registrants detect drift in post_restore without writing and repair it in their hook, which is ordered after emitter.place, with at most a one-run lag. Change V9 to position 6, slot restore (EmitterVerify) plus post_restore, and the clause to 'the pending set equals the live run's'. Add to KRN-RST-05 the D2.5 fixtures plus a late-hook upstream mutation fixture (Interaction M6 on a lit lamp's node on the snapshot tick).

cross_adr.text: ADR-0017 E1 (called by Web Map init_world under the INIT scope) calls M14 set_load_request for authored-on lamps. ADR-0012's mutator table allows M14 in APPLY and HOOK only, and its drain table has no INIT row.
cross_adr.amendment: Add INIT to M14's allowed scopes, with a drain-table row saying an INIT-scope deposit drains at the first graph.propagate.power execution of the first RUNNING step. State the tick stamp of the INIT pass so that ADR-0017's arm_tick formula has a defined T_a.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0017's I-BOUNDS and its segment-test overflow proof cite BODY_COORD_LIMIT from 'the ADR-0015 bounds ledger'. ADR-0015 defines only WORLD_COORD_LIMIT (2^22) and an informal 'tens of thousands of px' body-frame bound.
cross_adr.amendment: Add a named, data-held body-frame coordinate bound to the BodyTuning ledger (BODY_COORD_LIMIT, at most 2^24, derived from max section extent and max sections per body or enforced at attach). Add a boot or attach check, and cite it from the int32 column-sufficiency statement in section 11.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0017 E1 needs node_base(section_id) and the section template's emitter placements (def_id, anchor_x/y, node_ordinal, authored switch_on, subkind). ADR-0013 stores graph_ref_base but exposes no read for it, and defines no template accessor for emitter placements.
cross_adr.amendment: Add a Tier H node_base(section_id) -> int (0 = NONE, valid Class 1 after restore). Add a frozen SectionTemplates accessor set for emitter placements (emitter_placement_count(template_id) and indexed scalar getters), loaded at stage 1 with the template schema and validated against ItemCatalog emits.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0018 assumes the Emitter publishes the beam's occ_origin as a separate integer pair and reserves OCC_ORIGIN_MODE (FOOT). ADR-0017's EmitterView publishes only the chest origin and keeps occlusion_origin internal.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0017 adds occ_origin_x_of(id)/occ_origin_y_of(id) for BEAM rows and reserves the EmitterTuning row OCC_ORIGIN_MODE = FOOT. ADR-0018 then needs no change, and outcome D stays a one-function change.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0019's ControllerView publishes get_chest_point(player_id) -> Vector2i, get_aim_angle and get_loco_state. ADR-0017 assumes chest_point as two scalars and bare names, and justifies this with a false claim that SIM-03 bans Vector2i.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0017 consumes ADR-0019's names and the Vector2i return (a value type, allocation-free, SIM-03-legal). It updates its ADR-0019 assumption row and strikes the SIM-03 claim in D13.1.

cross_adr.text: The authoritative validate of PLAYER-origin set_switch (an Emitter command type) has no reach/focus, NOT_LIT or loco_state check. The GDDs assign NOT_LIT to Interaction, but under IA-3 Interaction has no validate on this command type.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0020 publishes a pure, allocation-free precondition read, for example InteractionView.verb_precondition(actor, subject_ref, verb) -> StringName returning NOT_LIT, OUT_OF_REACH or NOT_ACTIONABLE. ADR-0017's set_switch validate calls it for PLAYER origin, and its reasons pass through. ADR-0020 also confirms that Interaction never writes emitter.state from post_restore.

cross_adr.text: E9 create_seat_beam ('the new-game step') and E4 bind_beam ('once at new game') have no named caller. ADR-0017's ADR-0026 row lists only E1 then E10, and ADR-0016 records init_world as the only MVP world builder.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0026 names the new-game pass that calls E9 per bound seat and then Suit's E4 bind_beam, under the INIT scope, with an order relative to E1/E10. It also states that a restored run never calls them, since the binding comes from beam_bindings via binding_source.

findings.text: D2.5 defines pending states, but the combinations a late hook can produce in one tick are unspecified: E6 then E7 on a pending-register row, E7 then E6 on a pending-unregister row, E8 on a pending-register row, and a second E8 on a row that already has has_pend_anchor. data.verdict: CONCERNS. The core decisions hold up: one block and one hook, a pure integer kernel, a Q14/Q28 cone test, a doubled-coordinate slab segment test, a canonical hysteresis bit, an oracle-proven pair cache, counted work, and pending-intent columns. They are probed on the 4.7.2 editor binary and the alternatives are genuinely weighed. The problem statement, rationale and Consequences are honest, including the admission in D12.6 that the budget does not fit. What passes: the engine is stamped 4.7.2 with Knowledge Risk HIGH, post-cutoff APIs are listed and the probes are dated. All 57 TR rows that requirements-traceability.md maps to ADR-0017 are addressed, and all 46 TR-emitter rows are classified (42 decided, 15 shared, 9 owned elsewhere). Fault domain 6 matches the registry table. The rects_in / QueryBuffer.spans / version_epoch / changed_region usage matches ADR-0014 sections 5 and 6. The hook edges match ADR-0012 and ADR-0015, and the restore_after list matches ADR-0016 position 6. ADR-0004 lets each block number its own key kinds, so kind 1 is legal. Three blocking problems remain. (T1) The save-equivalence (G4) argument for post_restore is incomplete. Hooks ordered after emitter.place can write upstream blocks on the snapshot tick, for example Interaction calling Graph M6 (salvage_node). Re-running the hysteresis in post_restore can then rewrite a canonical lit bit. (T2) D10.2 has registrants re-register (E6) from their own post_restore. That is a cross-block canonical write, which ADR-0016 section 4.2 forbids. (T3) A PLAYER-origin set_switch has no reach, NOT_LIT or loco_state check anywhere on the authoritative path. Beyond those, several cross-ADR assumptions do not match the sibling drafts on disk: M14 is not allowed in the INIT scope, BODY_COORD_LIMIT does not exist, there is no node_base read and no template emitter-placement accessor, ControllerView names differ, and the published occ_origin is missing. These need amendment rows, not redesign.

findings.text: The G4 argument (D14.4 items 2-3, D9.5(b), D14.2) has a gap. It assumes post_restore re-derives the table from the same upstream state that the last emitter.place saw. That is not true when a hook ordered after emitter.place writes an upstream block on the snapshot tick. Concrete case: Interaction's hook runs after emitter.place (ADR-0017's own assumption on ADR-0020). It may call Graph M6 salvage_node, an immediate mutator allowed in HOOK scope (ADR-0012 scope table, and its assumption on ADR-0021 'M5/M6/M7 also from an Interaction hook'). The live run's table at the end of tick T still counts that lamp. The restored run's post_restore reads node_state SALVAGED, so the lamp is not live and act_lux drops. D14.2 then runs 'W6 with the hysteresis' and LitHysteresis.next(1, act') can write 0 into the canonical lit bit. The P2 validate at T+1 then accepts a lit-only verb in one run and rejects it NOT_LIT in the other. If act at T+1 sits between LIT_OFF_PM and LIT_ON_PM, the divergence persists. Writing a persisted column in post_restore also breaks ADR-0016 section 4.2. The 'idempotent' claim only holds for an identical act, and the late-hook mutation removes that.
findings.amendment: (1) In D9.5(b) and D14.2, make post_restore copy the lit bit verbatim and never call LitHysteresis.next. Only lux_pm, act_lux_pm, top_emitter_id and the record fields are recomputed. (2) Restate D14.4 (2)-(3): derived values rebuilt in post_restore reflect end-of-tick upstream state, which can differ from what the last run saw by any write made by a hook ordered after emitter.place. Only canonical-backed reads (lit, beam_of, subject_headroom, the registration set) are G4-exact before the first run. lux, top_emitter, output_of, r_lit_of, r_off_of and section_emission may differ for one run. Then add a rule plus a lint or test that no validate and no hook ordered before emitter.place decides state on those derived reads. Alternative to the read restriction: persist the per-emitter live/output inputs the last run used. (3) Add mandatory KRN-RST-05 fixtures to D2.5's list: Interaction's hook calls M6 on a lit lamp's node on the snapshot tick, and a late hook changes loco_state to DEAD on the snapshot tick.

findings.text: D10.2 says registrants (Interaction, Horror, loot spawners) 're-register idempotently in their own post_restore (restore_after allows it)', and the ADR-0020 cross-ADR row repeats it. E6/E7/E8 write canonical emitter.state columns (D2.5) and must begin with scope.open_for (D3.4, EMT-05). Under ADR-0016 section 4.2 and its line 347, post_restore holds no WriteScope and must never write another block. ADR-0016 (lines 392 and 418) already moved Interaction to 'detect at post_restore, repair in the hook'. This text cannot be implemented and conflicts with a sibling. It also muddies Open Question 4.
findings.amendment: Rewrite D10.2: registrations are canonical and restore verbatim, so a well-formed save needs no re-registration. A registrant detects drift in its own post_restore without writing, and repairs it in its first hook run through E6/E7/E8. The pending columns of D2.5 absorb the repair with at most a one-run lag. Apply the same wording to the ADR-0020 and ADR-0022/0023 rows in Cross-ADR Assumptions. Close Open Question 4 on that basis, keeping 'no edge from Interaction' and 'Interaction ordered after emitter.place'.

findings.text: D3.2/D3.3 give PLAYER-origin set_switch the validation order NO_SUCH_EMITTER, NOT_SWITCHABLE, COOLDOWN only. The GDD (EM set_switch row; Interaction line 136, IA-37) says 'NOT_LIT is Interaction's own precondition'. Under IA-3 and ADR-0002, a command type has exactly one validate, and set_switch's validate is the Emitter's. The payload is {emitter_id} only. No step of the authoritative pipeline therefore checks reach or focus, NOT_LIT, or a DEAD/DOWNED/STAGGERED actor for a fixture switch, although toggle_beam has NOT_ACTIONABLE. A PLAYER submit can switch any fixture by id from anywhere, and in VS-B a remote peer can too. Stories for the verb cannot be cut without knowing where those checks live.
findings.amendment: In D3.2, add to the PLAYER set_switch order (before COOLDOWN) a call to a pure Interaction-published precondition, for example InteractionView.verb_precondition(actor, subject_ref, verb) -> StringName, returning NOT_LIT, OUT_OF_REACH or NOT_ACTIONABLE. Its reasons pass through under VALIDATION_FAILED. This keeps IA-11(a), which forbids reading node health. State that the Emitter owns the call site and ADR-0020 owns the predicate (see the cross-ADR item). If the decision is instead that the Adapter's focus filter is sufficient, say so explicitly and record the authority consequence for VS-B.

Delete the 'restore-time leaf bump is REGION, not ALL' sentence.

findings.text: D2.5 defines pending states, but the combinations a late hook can produce in one tick are unspecified: E6 then E7 on a pending-register row, E7 then E6 on a pending-unregister row, E8 on a pending-register row, and a second E8 on a row that already has has_pend_anchor. Each changes caps, subject_headroom and restore validation (EMITTER_RESTORE_SUBJECTS), so a story cannot be cut without it. The transition table of D3.6 covers the record lifecycle and the lit bit, not pending.
findings.amendment: Add a TRANSITIONS_PENDING table to emitter_kind.gd. E6+E7 on pending 1 drops the row with no table effect. E7 on 2 is a no-op. E6 on 2 returns to 0 with an unchanged anchor, or 0 with a pending anchor if the anchor differs, and reports DUPLICATE. E8 on pending 1 writes the applied anchor directly. A repeated E8 overwrites pend_x/pend_y. Add the cases to the D2.5 fixture list.

findings.text: Wording errors that a story would copy. (a) D14.2 'so no subject is pending when the first validate runs' (inherited from ADR-0016 V9) contradicts D2.5: rows pending at the snapshot stay pending until W3 of T+1, as in the live run. (b) D14.3 places V9 at 'DAG position 5', but the ADR-0016 table has emitter.state at position 6, and its V9 slot is post_restore while D14.3 calls EmitterVerify from restore. (c) D4.2 says the derived columns are written only inside emitter.place, but E10 (P2) and the creation mutators (any scope) also write derived record fields. (d) D6.4 says reconciliation happens 'on the tick after its phase 11 ran', but emitter.place is after graph.propagate.failure on the same tick, which is what 'never later' (TR-ftrail-041) needs.
findings.amendment: (a) Reword to 'the pending set equals the live run's at T+1'. (b) Say position 6, slot restore (EmitterVerify) plus post_restore (rebuild). (c) List E10 and the creation mutators as the only out-of-hook derived writers. (d) Say 'in the same tick, after the failure hook completes'.

findings.text: Mandatory block callables and call sites are missing. default_state is mandatory (ADR-0003 section 2, line 97) and D2.1 does not specify it, while ADR-0016 asks each owner for a default_state its own restore accepts. E9 create_seat_beam is called from 'the new-game step' and E4 bind_beam 'once at new game', but no owner or order relative to Web Map's E1/E10 is named.
findings.amendment: In D2.1, add default_state: empty columns, next_emitter_id 1, last_place_tick -1, fault_step_seen -1, passing EmitterVerify. Name the E9/E4 call site and its order relative to E1/E10 (see the cross-ADR item on ADR-0026).

findings.text: HOT-01 scoping. D6.4 reads LayoutView.anchor_geometry (Tier C, allocates, per ADR-0013) and FailureSlice-driven creation inside W1. The Implementation Guidelines tag '_hook_place and its W-step helpers' ## @hot, so the fault-glow creation path would trip HOT-01 or CNT-01 whenever a glow is created.
findings.amendment: State that FAULT_GLOW row creation and removal, E1/E2 and slot-store insert/remove are untagged cold helpers called from the tagged W1. Scope CNT-01 to ticks with no structural change, or have the 600-tick fixture include a steady fault set.

findings.text: Traceability ownership error: the 'Shared' table lists TR-interact-038 with ADR-0012 as the other owner. ADR-0012's own row hands the Interaction hook budget to 'ADR-0017/0020'.
findings.amendment: Change the other owner of TR-interact-038 to ADR-0020 (the Interaction hook's own budget and worst-case load). This ADR keeps the Emitter's share and lit() as a table lookup.

findings.text: Right-sizing for a solo MVP. Two slot stores, per-section point grids, stride-K pair rows, static_epoch mover sweeps, an always-on tally, 22 fault codes and an 8-rule lint pack are justified only by a D.14 cost model whose weights are unverified. The Migration Plan already builds the brute-force oracle path first (step 6) but makes the optimised step 7 unconditional.
findings.amendment: Make Migration step 7 (grids, pair rows, static_epoch) conditional on step 6 measured against B on the S1 harness. If the oracle/cold-build path meets B with margin at the typical point, ship it and keep steps 7 and onward as ladder rungs behind the same API. Keep the transparency fuzz as the entry condition for step 7.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0016's assumption on ADR-0017 ('emitter.place is ordered after the Interaction hook that repairs subject drift') and its Open Question 5 contradict ADR-0017 D3.1 and Open Question 4. ADR-0017 declares no edge from Interaction and orders Interaction after emitter.place, because E3 at the landing tick and the D2.5 late-hook semantics depend on it. ADR-0016's V9 row also says 'no subject pending at the first validate', which D2.5 makes false by design.
cross_adr.amendment: Close Open Question 5 with ADR-0017's position: registrations are canonical; registrants detect drift in post_restore without writing and repair it in their hook, which is ordered after emitter.place, with at most a one-run lag. Change V9 to position 6, slot restore (EmitterVerify) plus post_restore, and the clause to 'the pending set equals the live run's'. Add to KRN-RST-05 the D2.5 fixtures plus a late-hook upstream mutation fixture (Interaction M6 on a lit lamp's node on the snapshot tick).

cross_adr.text: ADR-0017 E1 (called by Web Map init_world under the INIT scope) calls M14 set_load_request for authored-on lamps. ADR-0012's mutator table allows M14 in APPLY and HOOK only, and its drain table has no INIT row.
cross_adr.amendment: Add INIT to M14's allowed scopes, with a drain-table row saying an INIT-scope deposit drains at the first graph.propagate.power execution of the first RUNNING step. State the tick stamp of the INIT pass so that ADR-0017's arm_tick formula has a defined T_a.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0017's I-BOUNDS and its segment-test overflow proof cite BODY_COORD_LIMIT from 'the ADR-0015 bounds ledger'. ADR-0015 defines only WORLD_COORD_LIMIT (2^22) and an informal 'tens of thousands of px' body-frame bound.
cross_adr.amendment: Add a named, data-held body-frame coordinate bound to the BodyTuning ledger (BODY_COORD_LIMIT, at most 2^24, derived from max section extent and max sections per body or enforced at attach). Add a boot or attach check, and cite it from the int32 column-sufficiency statement in section 11.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0017 E1 needs node_base(section_id) and the section template's emitter placements (def_id, anchor_x/y, node_ordinal, authored switch_on, subkind). ADR-0013 stores graph_ref_base but exposes no read for it, and defines no template accessor for emitter placements.
cross_adr.amendment: Add a Tier H node_base(section_id) -> int (0 = NONE, valid Class 1 after restore). Add a frozen SectionTemplates accessor set for emitter placements (emitter_placement_count(template_id) and indexed scalar getters), loaded at stage 1 with the template schema and validated against ItemCatalog emits.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0018 assumes the Emitter publishes the beam's occ_origin as a separate integer pair and reserves OCC_ORIGIN_MODE (FOOT). ADR-0017's EmitterView publishes only the chest origin and keeps occlusion_origin internal.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0017 adds occ_origin_x_of(id)/occ_origin_y_of(id) for BEAM rows and reserves the EmitterTuning row OCC_ORIGIN_MODE = FOOT. ADR-0018 then needs no change, and outcome D stays a one-function change.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0019's ControllerView publishes get_chest_point(player_id) -> Vector2i, get_aim_angle and get_loco_state. ADR-0017 assumes chest_point as two scalars and bare names, and justifies this with a false claim that SIM-03 bans Vector2i.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0017 consumes ADR-0019's names and the Vector2i return (a value type, allocation-free, SIM-03-legal). It updates its ADR-0019 assumption row and strikes the SIM-03 claim in D13.1.

cross_adr.text: The authoritative validate of PLAYER-origin set_switch (an Emitter command type) has no reach/focus, NOT_LIT or loco_state check. The GDDs assign NOT_LIT to Interaction, but under IA-3 Interaction has no validate on this command type.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0020 publishes a pure, allocation-free precondition read, for example InteractionView.verb_precondition(actor, subject_ref, verb) -> StringName returning NOT_LIT, OUT_OF_REACH or NOT_ACTIONABLE. ADR-0017's set_switch validate calls it for PLAYER origin, and its reasons pass through. ADR-0020 also confirms that Interaction never writes emitter.state from post_restore.

cross_adr.text: E9 create_seat_beam ('the new-game step') and E4 bind_beam ('once at new game') have no named caller. ADR-0017's ADR-0026 row lists only E1 then E10, and ADR-0016 records init_world as the only MVP world builder.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0026 names the new-game pass that calls E9 per bound seat and then Suit's E4 bind_beam, under the INIT scope, with an order relative to E1/E10. It also states that a restored run never calls them, since the binding comes from beam_bindings via binding_source.
